rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “from him” may refer to Joseph, meaning they despaired of his releasing their brother, or to their brother, meaning they despaired of him.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنها ترجع إلى يوسف فالمعنى يئسوا من يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They withdrew from other people to confer and deliberate alone; najiyyan is singular because it functions as a verbal noun that has one form for dual, plural, and feminine.
rows.anchor: اعتزلوا الناس ليس معهم غيرهم يتناجون ويتناظرون ويتشاورون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He explains their becoming alone as their conferring about what to do when returning to their father, without their brother.
rows.anchor: انفردوا متناجين فيما يعملون في ذهابهم إلى أبيهم وليس معهم أخوهم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The eldest in judgment was Judah, though Reuben was the oldest by age.
rows.anchor: أنه يهوذا ولم يكن أكبرهم سنا وإنما كان أكبرهم سنا روبيل

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: They identify Judah as the eldest in judgment, distinguishing him from Reuben, the oldest by age.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال الضحاك ومقاتل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He identifies Simon as the eldest in judgment.
rows.anchor: أنه شمعون قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: They take “their eldest” to mean the eldest by age, Reuben.
rows.anchor: أنه كبيرهم في السن وهو روبيل قاله قتادة والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant their father took from them concerned protecting their brother and bringing him back.
rows.anchor: أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثق من الله ) في حفظ أخيكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The particle mā may be nominative: the meaning is that their earlier neglect of Joseph was already established.
rows.anchor: ما في موضع رفع كأنه قال ومن قبل هذا تفريطكم في يوسف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā may be accusative, meaning they already knew of their neglect of Joseph.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت جعلتها نصبا المعنى ألم تعلموا هذا وتعلموا من قبل تفريطكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: A third parse treats mā as extra, yielding “you neglected Joseph before”; al-Zajjaj calls this the strongest analysis.
rows.anchor: جعلت ما صلة كأنه قال ومن قبل فرطتم في يوسف قال الزجاج وهذا أجود الوجوه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He prefers treating mā as an expendable particle in the phrase about the brothers’ earlier neglect of Joseph.
rows.anchor: وهذا أجود الوجوه أن تكون ما لغوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I will not leave the land” means the eldest brother will not leave the land of Egypt.
rows.anchor: أي لن أخرج من أرض مصر يقال برح الرجل براحا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets “until my father permits me” as waiting for his father to send word that he may come.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس حتى يبعث إلي أن آتيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s judgment may mean returning the brother, granting victory by the sword against his captor, or decreeing some outcome in the speaker’s case.
rows.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أو يحكم الله لي فيرد أخي علي والثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the most just and excellent of judges.
rows.anchor: ( وهو خير الحاكمين ) أي أعدلهم وأفضلهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وابن أبي سريج عن الكسائي
rows.claim: They read sariqa with a rounded initial sīn, a doubled rāʾ, and kasra, rather than the familiar reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والضحاك وابن أبي سريج عن الكسائي سرق بضم السين

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The brothers testified to theft only from what they knew: they had seen the stolen object in Benjamin’s baggage.
rows.anchor: وما شهدنا عليه بالسرقة إلا بما علمنا لأنا رأينا المسروق في رحله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: They testified about Joseph’s rule that a thief is taken for his theft because they knew their father’s law.
rows.anchor: وما شهدنا عن يوسف بأن السارق يؤخذ بسرقته إلا بما علمنا من دينك

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: “We were not guardians of the unseen” can mean they did not know what Benjamin had done during the night, suggesting the accusation arose at night.
rows.anchor: أن الغيب هو الليل والمعنى لم نعلم ما صنع بالليل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They did not know that their brother would steal; Ibn Qutayba explains that they had not known this when pledging to return him.
rows.anchor: ما كنا نعلم أن ابنك يسرق رواه ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They could not keep Benjamin safe from theft.
rows.anchor: لم نستطع أن نحفظه فلا يسرق رواه عبد الوهاب عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: They did not know that Benjamin stole something belonging to the king, which is why they judged the thief enslaved.
rows.anchor: لم نعلم أنه سرق للملك شيئا ولذلك حكمنا باسترقاق السارق

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Although they saw the theft from his baggage, they had no knowledge of the unseen and could not rule out that others planted it.
rows.anchor: قد رأينا السرقة قد أخذت من رحله ولا علم لنا بالغيب فلعلهم سرقوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could guard their brother only while he was present; his affairs became hidden from them when absent.
rows.anchor: إنما نقدر على حفظه في محضره فإذا غاب عنا خفيت عنا أموره

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: They would not have travelled with Benjamin if they had known this calamity would befall him.
rows.anchor: لو علمنا من الغيب أن هذه البلية تقع بابنك ما سافرنا به

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: They did not know Jacob would suffer this loss as he had suffered Joseph’s; had they known, they would not have taken Benjamin.
rows.anchor: لم نعلم أنك تصاب به كما أصبت بيوسف ولو علمنا لم نذهب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers mean that their father should ask the people of the town, namely Egypt.
rows.anchor: المعنى قولوا لأبيكم سل أهل القرية ( التي كنا فيها ) يعنون مصر

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The caravan means its people, including Canaanites who had travelled with the brothers.
rows.anchor: وكان قد صحبهم قوم من الكنعانيين قال ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Alternatively, the town and caravan themselves can be asked because prophets may address speaking stones and animals, avoiding an omitted “people.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى وسل القرية والعير فإنها تعقل عنك لأنك نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech is compressed: the sons returned, told Jacob what happened, and Jacob replied; the fuller account was given at 12:18.
rows.anchor: في الكلام اختصار والمعنى فرجعوا إلى أبيهم فقالوا له ذلك فقال لهم هذا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Jacob suspected the absent son’s brothers had left him behind through a scheme intended to make their story believable.
rows.anchor: أنه ظن أن الذي تخلف منهم إنما تخلف حيلة ومكرا ليصدقهم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He means they thought taking Benjamin would bring benefit, but it instead brought harm.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى سولت لكم أنفسكم أن خروجكم بأخيكم يجلب نفعا فجر ضررا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that their own selves persuaded them that Benjamin had stolen when he had not.
rows.anchor: سولت لكم أنه سرق وما سرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob hopes God will bring him Joseph, Benjamin, and the other brother who stayed in Egypt.
rows.anchor: يعني يوسف وبنيامين وأخاهما المقيم بمصر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He specifies Judah and Simon as the two who remained in Egypt, making four sons Jacob hopes to see.
rows.anchor: أقام بمصر يهوذا وشمعون فاراد بقوله أن يأتيني بهم يعني الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Knowing” refers either to God’s knowledge of Jacob’s intense grief or to His knowledge of the brothers’ location.
rows.anchor: أي بشدة حزني وقيل بمكانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Wise” means God is wise in what He has decreed for Jacob.
rows.anchor: ( الحكيم ) فيما حكم علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turned away from his sons to avoid prolonging the discussion and withdrew into grief, renewing his remembrance of Joseph.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن ولده أن يطيل معهم الخطب وانفرد بحزنه وهيج عليه ذكر يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “Alas for Joseph” means, “How long my grief for Joseph!”
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يا طول حزني على يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Asaf is the most intense form of regret and sorrow.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة الأسف أشد الحسرة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: At calamity this community was given the words “We belong to God and to Him we return,” which earlier prophets had not received; Jacob would have used them.
rows.anchor: لقد أعطيت هذه الأمة عند المصيبة مالم يعط الأنبياء قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s lament is compatible with patience because he complained to God, not against God; alternatively, he meant it as a prayer for mercy on his grief.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه شكا إلى الله تعالى لا منه والثاني أنه أراد به الدعاء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The vocative is figurative: Jacob addresses grief in wording while meaning, “My God, have mercy on my grief,” or “You see my grief.”
rows.anchor: نداء يعقوب الأسف في اللفظ من المجاز الذي يعني به غير المظهر في اللفظ

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Grief and inward aversion to calamity are neither blameworthy nor sinful unless the tongue utters sinful speech; Jacob complained only to his Lord.
rows.anchor: والحزن ونفور النفس من المكروه والبلاء لا عيب فيه ولا مأثم إذا لم ينطق اللسان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When his brother died and he grieved intensely, al-Hasan defended himself by noting that God did not blame Jacob’s grief for Joseph.
rows.anchor: ما وجدت الله عاب على يعقوب الحزن حيث قال يا أسفي على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes disagree whether Jacob became blind or only had weakened sight under the whiteness caused by much weeping.
rows.anchor: أي انقلبت إلى حال البياض وهل ذهب بصره أم لا فيه قولان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Jacob lost his sight.
rows.anchor: أنه ذهب بصره قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: His sight weakened because a whiteness covered his eyes from extensive crying; Muqatil says he could not see for six years.
rows.anchor: ضعف بصره لبياض تغشاه من كثرة البكاء ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “From grief” means from weeping: the cause, grief, is named for its effect, tears.
rows.anchor: وقوله من الحزن أي من البكاء يريد أن عينيه ابيضتا لكثرة بكائه

rows.speaker: ثابت البناني
rows.claim: In a report, Gabriel tells Joseph that Jacob’s grief equalled that of seventy bereaved mothers and earned one hundred martyrs’ reward.
rows.anchor: حزن سبعين ثكلى قال فهل له على ذلك من أجر قال أجر مائة شهيد

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Jacob remained grief-stricken for eighty years, never dried his eyes, and was then especially dear to God when he lost his sight.
rows.anchor: ما فارق يعقوب الحزن ثمانين سنة وما جفت عينه وما أحد يومئذ أكرم على الله منه

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Kẓīm means one who restrains and conceals his grief rather than displaying it.
rows.anchor: الكظيم بمعنى الكاظم وهو الممسك على حزنه فلا يظهره

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The oath’s answer contains an implicit lā: “By God, you will not cease”; Arabs omit the understood negative, as the cited poets do.
rows.anchor: معناه والله وجواب هذا القسم لا المضمرة التي تأويلها تالله لا تفتأ

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: His oath-poem’s abraḥ witnesses the omitted negative: “I will never cease sitting,” meaning “I will not leave off.”
rows.anchor: فقلت يمين الله أبرح قاعدا ولو قطعوا رأسي لديك وأوصالي

rows.speaker: الخنساء
rows.claim: Her oath-poem’s āsā similarly means “I will not grieve.”
rows.anchor: فأقسمت آسى على هالك أو اسأل نائحة مالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic example likewise uses “I forget my loss” to mean “I will never forget.”
rows.anchor: تالله أنسى مصيبتي أبدا ما أسمعتني حنينها الإبل

rows.speaker: أبو عمران وابن محيصن وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: They read the oath with bāʾ, “By God,” instead of tāʾ; the source says this reading occurs in each Quranic oath.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمران وابن محيصن وأبو حيوة قالوا بالله بالباء

rows.speaker: المفسرون وأهل اللغة
rows.claim: Tafsir and language authorities explain taftaʾ as “you do not cease,” so the sons say Jacob keeps remembering Joseph.
rows.anchor: معنى تفتأ تزال فمعنى الكلام لا تزال تذكر يوسف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: His cited poem uses faʾat to attest the sense “did not cease” for taftaʾ.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة فما فتئت خيل تثوب وتدعي ويلحق منها

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: His cited verse uses faʾat of bands of birds that kept gathering until reaching Banu Sakhr.
rows.anchor: وأنشد ابن القاسم فما فتئت منا رعال كأنها رعال القطا

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ḥaraḍ means sickly and weakened by grief; Ibn Qutayba glosses it as made ill, while Abu Ubayda says grief or love has melted the person.
rows.anchor: أنه الدنف قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال ابن قتيبة يقال أحرضه الحزن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: His poem uses aḥraḍanī for love melting and wasting the speaker until sickness consumed him.
rows.anchor: وأنشد إني امرؤ لج بي حب فأحرضني حتى بليت وحتى شفني السقم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says ḥaraḍ is bodily corruption, yielding the sense “until you become sick and debilitated.”
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج الحرض الفاسد في جسمه والمعنى حتى تكون مدنفا مريضا

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ḥaraḍ means a person whose reason has gone; Ibn Ishaq likewise calls it mental corruption.
rows.anchor: أنه الذاهب العقل قاله الضحاك عن ابن عباس وقال ابن إسحق الفاسد العقل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He allows ḥaraḍ to mean corruption of a person’s character.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وقد يكون الحرض الفاسد في أخلاقه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Ḥāriḍ denotes bodily and mental corruption, while ḥaraḍ is a verbal noun that does not inflect for number or gender.
rows.anchor: والثالث أنه الفاسد في جسمه وعقله يقال رجل حارض وحرض

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: They interpret ḥaraḍ as old age.
rows.anchor: أنه الهرم قاله الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among the perishing” means among the dead.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ( أو تكون من الهالكين ) يعنون الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons’ oath is qualified by an understood phrase: this was according to their estimation and expectation.
rows.anchor: أن في الكلام إضمارا تقديره إن هذا في تقديرنا وظننا

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Bathth is intense grief, named for the sufferer’s inability to bear it without voicing it.
rows.anchor: البث أشد الحزن سمي بذلك لأن صاحبه لا يصبر عليه حتى يبثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob means he complains to God rather than to his sons, in response to their reproach.
rows.anchor: ( إلى الله ) المعنى إني لا أشكو إليكم وذلك لما عنفوه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted from Anas and included by al-Hakim in his Ṣaḥīḥ recounts Gabriel’s message to Jacob: his blindness came from weeping for Joseph and his bent back from grief over Benjamin; God reproached him for complaining elsewhere, then promised to reunite him with his sons if dead, and urged feeding the poor. Jacob thereafter invited poor and fasting people to his meals.
rows.anchor: وروى الحاكم أبو عبد الله في صحيحه من حديث أنس بن مالك عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: A revelation says Jacob’s long separation resulted from withholding food from a fasting poor neighbor after slaughtering an ewe; another report says he slaughtered a calf before its distressed mother without pity.
rows.anchor: أوحى الله تعالى إلى يعقوب أتدري لم عاقبتك وجبست عنك يوسف ثمانين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reason Joseph did not summon his father as soon as he became king has three explanations; the author prefers that God ordered the delay to raise Jacob’s rank through patience, while Joseph also grieved at his father’s pain.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل كيف صبر يوسف عن أبيه بعد أن صار ملكا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jacob knew Joseph’s dream was true and that the family would prostrate to him.
rows.anchor: أعلم أن رؤيا يوسف صادقة وأنا سنسجد له رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن السائب
rows.claim: Jacob knew Joseph remained alive: when he asked the Angel of Death whether he had taken Joseph’s soul, the angel said no.
rows.anchor: أعلم من سلامة يوسف مالا تعلمون قال ابن السائب وذلك أن ملك الموت أتاه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Jacob knew more about God’s mercy and power than his sons did.
rows.anchor: أعلم من رحمة الله وقدرته مالا تعلمون قاله عطاء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: After hearing how the ruler treated his sons, Jacob hoped the ruler was Joseph; this explains his order to search.
rows.anchor: لما أخبره بنوه بسيرة العزيز طمع أن يكون هو يوسف قاله السدي

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: After the Angel of Death said Joseph was not dead, Jacob became hopeful and sent his sons to seek Joseph and Benjamin.
rows.anchor: لما قال له ملك الموت ما قبضت روح يوسف تباشر عند ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Taḥassasū means to seek information and search likely places.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة تحسسوا أي تخبروا والتمسوا في المظان

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The preposition min may substitute for ʿan, so the command means to seek news about Joseph.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى عن يوسف ولكن نابت عنها من

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Alternatively min is partitive: seek some report about Joseph.
rows.anchor: أن من أوثرت للتبعيض والمعنى تحسسوا خبرا من أخبار يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: They take God’s rūḥ here as His mercy.
rows.anchor: من رحمة الله قاله ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He interprets rūḥ as relief from distress.
rows.anchor: من فرج الله قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: He interprets rūḥ as God’s enlargement or provision.
rows.anchor: من توسعة الله حكاه ابن القاسم

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Rūḥ means respite and relief from anguish in the heart.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي الروح الاستراحة من غم القلب

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: They understand the phrase as the relief God brings; believers hope in God during hardship, whereas disbelievers despair.
rows.anchor: لأن المؤمن يرجوا الله في الشدائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account omits their journey back to Egypt before they entered Joseph’s presence; al-ʿAzīz was the title used for their king.
rows.anchor: في الكلام محذوف تقديره فخرجوا إلى مصر فدخلوا على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea that hardship struck them and their family refers to poverty and need.
rows.anchor: ( مسنا وأهلنا الضر ) يعنون الفقر والحاجة

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The brothers’ meager merchandise consisted of dirhams.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت دراهم رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: It consisted of worn goods such as a rope and a sack.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت متاعا رثا كالحبل والغرارة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: It consisted of dried curds.
rows.anchor: كانت أقطا قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: جويبر عن الضحاك
rows.claim: It consisted of shoes and leather goods.
rows.anchor: كانت نعالا وأدما رواه جويبر عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another report says their goods consisted of mash made from al-muql fruit.
rows.anchor: كانت سويق المقل روي عن الضحاك أيضا

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Their merchandise was green grain and pine nuts.
rows.anchor: حبة الخضراء وصنوبر قاله أبو صالح

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
rows.claim: Their merchandise consisted of wool and some clarified butter.
rows.anchor: كانت صوفا وشيئا من سمن قاله عبد الله بن الحارث

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن إسحاق وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Muzjāh means small or insignificant: they brought little money with which they could barely sustain themselves; al-Zajjaj derives it from pushing along a meager livelihood.
rows.anchor: أنها القليلة روى العوفي عن ابن عباس قال دراهم غير طائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited rajaz poem uses tuzjī for a camel pushing its young along behind it, illustrating the sense of driving or sustaining.
rows.anchor: الواهب المائة الهجان وعبدها عوذا تزجي خلفها أطفالها

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muzjāh can mean shoddy, rejected goods; Abu Ubayda derives it from being pushed away as unacceptable.
rows.anchor: أنها الرديئة رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: His cited poem uses tuzjī for an impoverished widow who drives a destitute person through the night.
rows.anchor: وأنشد ليبك على ملحان ضيف مدفع وأرملة تزجي من الليل أرملا

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another reported sense of muzjāh is stagnant or unsalable goods.
rows.anchor: والثالث الكاسدة رواه الضحاك أيضا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another reported sense is worn-out merchandise.
rows.anchor: والرابع الرثة وهي المتاع الخلق

rows.speaker: أبو حصين عن عكرمة
rows.claim: Another reported sense is deficient or incomplete goods.
rows.anchor: والخامس الناقصة رواه أبو حصين عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask Joseph to complete the measure, not reduce it because their merchandise is poor.
rows.anchor: أي أتمه لنا ولا تنقصه لرداءة بضاعتنا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والسدي
rows.claim: “Give charity” asks Joseph to overlook the difference between the value of good and defective goods; Ibn al-Anbari says the concession only resembles charity.
rows.anchor: تصدق علينا بما بين سعر الجياد والرديئة قاله سعيد بن جبير والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: They ask Joseph to return their brother; Ibn Jurayj says they were prophets, for whom alms were forbidden.
rows.anchor: برد أخينا قال ابن جريج قال وذلك أنهم كانوا أنبياء والصدقة لا تحل

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: They ask for an amount beyond their due measure; this view holds that alms were lawful for prophets before Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وتصدق علينا بالزيادة على حقنا قاله ابن عيينة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: They say God rewards those who give charity, not “if you give us charity,” because they did not know Joseph was a believer.
rows.anchor: لم يقولوا إن الله يجزيك إن تصدقت علينا لأنهم لم يعلموا أنه مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards charitable people with recompense.
rows.anchor: أي بالثواب قال الضحاك لم يقولوا إن الله يجزيك

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Joseph showed his brothers their written promise to sell him; they recognized it, and, as he ordered them to be killed, Judah reminded a brother that Jacob could not bear losing them all, so Joseph relented and revealed himself.
rows.anchor: أخرج إليهم نسخة الكتاب الذي كتبوه على أنفسهم ببيعه من مالك بن ذعر

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: When they described their family’s hardship, Joseph felt compassion and asked whether they knew what they had done to him and his brother.
rows.anchor: لما قالوا مسنا وأهلنا الضر أدركته الرحمة فقال لهم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account says Jacob wrote that if Joseph did not return his son, a curse would reach the seventh generation; Joseph wept and spoke to them.
rows.anchor: إن يعقوب كتب إليه كتابا إن رددت ولدي وإلا دعوت عليك دعوة تدرك السابع

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Hal may be rhetorical rather than a genuine question: Joseph means, “How terrible was what you did,” especially the severing of kinship and violation of right.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنها استفهام لتعظيم القصة لا يراد به نفس الاستفهام

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Alternatively, the rhetorical question asks whether they knew the outcome: God delivered Joseph and Benjamin from harm, confirming the earlier promise that they would be told of their deed.
rows.anchor: هل علمتم عقبى ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه من تسليم الله لهما من المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes take hal to mean qad, “already.”
rows.anchor: والثاني أن هل بمعنى قد ذكره بعض أهل التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers also wronged Benjamin by separating him from Joseph, harming him after Joseph disappeared, and insulting him when he was accused of stealing.
rows.anchor: أحدها أنهم فرقوا بينه وبين يوسف فنغصوا عيشه بذلك والثاني أنهم آذوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “When you were ignorant” means when the brothers were children.
rows.anchor: إذ أنتم صبيان قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The phrase means “when you were sinful.”
rows.anchor: مذنبون قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: It means they were ignorant of disobeying their father, severing kinship, and following their desires.
rows.anchor: جاهلون بعقوق الأب وقطع الرحم وموافقة الهوى

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Alternatively, they were ignorant of how Joseph’s affair would turn out.
rows.anchor: جاهلون بما يؤول إليه أمر يوسف ذكرهما ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The brothers say God preferred Joseph in kingship.
rows.anchor: بالملك قاله الضحاك عن ابن عباس والثاني بالصبر

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They say God preferred Joseph for his patience.
rows.anchor: بالصبر قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: They say God preferred Joseph for his forbearance and forgiveness toward them.
rows.anchor: بالحلم والصفح عنا ذكره أبو سليمان الدمشقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation includes Joseph’s knowledge, intelligence, beauty, and the other virtues he was given.
rows.anchor: بالعلم والعقل والحسن وسائر الفضائل التي أعطاه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The brothers admit they were sinners and guilty regarding Joseph.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس لمذنبين آثمين في أمرك قال ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾīn was chosen over mukhṭiʾīn because the former means sinful, while the latter means merely missing the right course without sin.
rows.anchor: معنى خطئ يخطأ فهو خاطئ آثم ومعنى أخطأ يخطئ فهو مخطئ ترك الصواب

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The form khāṭiʾīn may also have been chosen to match the verse endings.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون آثر خاطئين على مخطئين لموافقة رؤوس الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ gives two senses for in: “although we were sinners” or “we were only sinners.”
rows.anchor: وذكر الفراء في معنى إن قولين أحدهما وقد كنا خاطئين

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Joseph promises not to reproach his brothers for this ever again.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح عن ابن عباس لا أعيركم بعد اليوم بهذا أبدا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Joseph specifies “today” because it is the first moment of pardon, when one who forgives should not revisit punishment.
rows.anchor: إنما أشار إلى ذلك اليوم لأنه أول أوقات العفو وسبيل العافي في مثله أن لا يراجع عقوبة

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: The verb tharraba means to enumerate someone’s sins against them.
rows.anchor: قد ثرب فلان على فلان إذا عدد عليه ذنوبه

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He glosses the phrase as no blaming after that day and traces taṯrīb to corruption or spoiling.
rows.anchor: لا تعيير عليكم بعد هذا اليوم بما صنعتم وأصل التثريب الإفساد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith instructs that if a slave woman commits adultery she is to be flogged, but not reproached afterward.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليجلدها الحد ولا يثرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Joseph absolved them and asked God to forgive them.
rows.anchor: جعلهم في حل وسأل الله المغفرة لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Fannada means to regard someone as ignorant.
rows.anchor: تجهلون رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: It may mean to call someone foolish; another report from Mujahid says Jacob’s sons feared others would say he had lost his reason.
rows.anchor: تسفهون رواه عبد الله بن أبي الهذيل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك
rows.claim: Fannada can mean to accuse Jacob of lying.
rows.anchor: تكذبون رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: It can mean senile; Ibn Faris traces al-fand to loss of reason in old age.
rows.anchor: تهرمون قاله الحسن ومجاهد في رواية قال ابن فارس

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Fannada may mean to make someone incapable.
rows.anchor: تعجزون قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He groups foolishness, incapacity, and blame together and cites poetry using tafnīd for reproach.
rows.anchor: تسفهون وتعجزون وتلومون وأنشد يا صاحبي دعا لومي وتفنيدي

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: He says the root sense is corruption and that the exegetes’ interpretations are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: وأصل التفنيد الإفساد وأقوال المفسرين تتقارب معانيها

rows.speaker: أبو محمد ابن الخشاب
rows.claim: He says the statement contains an ellipsis: Jacob means, “Were it not that you would accuse me, I would tell you he is alive.”
rows.anchor: لولا أن تفندون فيه إضمار تقديره لأخبرتكم أنه حي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Jacob’s grandchildren, rather than his sons, addressed him as being in his old delusion.
rows.anchor: بنو بنيه خاطبوه بهذا وكذلك قال السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
rows.claim: His “old delusion” means error.
rows.anchor: أنه بمعنى الخطأ قاله ابن عباس وابن زيد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The phrase means madness.
rows.anchor: أنه الجنون قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: It means worldly misery and hardship.
rows.anchor: الشقاء والعناء قاله مقاتل يريد بذلك شقاء الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس ووهب بن منبه والسدي والجمهور
rows.claim: The bearer of good news was Judah.
rows.anchor: أنه يهوذا قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال وهب بن منبه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He identifies the bearer of good news as Simon.
rows.anchor: أنه سمعون قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Adding an to “when he came” and omitting it elsewhere are both Quraysh usages; an emphasizes the completed past, while the bare verb already makes the past clear.
rows.anchor: هما لغتان لقريش خاطبهم الله بهما جميعا فدخول أن لتوكيد مضي الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearer laid the shirt on Jacob’s face, and Jacob regained his sight; irtadda means that something returns to its former state.
rows.anchor: الارتداد رجوع الشيء إلى حال قد كان عليها

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Irtadda, rather than “was returned,” is used because the verb can be attributed to the affected object, as in a tree moving versus God moving it.
rows.anchor: إنما قال ارتد ولم يقل رد لأن هذا من الأفعال المنسوبة إلى المفعولين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Jacob’s sight, strength, youth, and happiness returned after blindness, weakness, old age, and sorrow.
rows.anchor: رجع إليه بصره بعد العمى وقوته بعد الضعف وشبابه بعد الهرم

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: In a report through Yaḥyā ibn Yamān, Jacob asked what faith Joseph had maintained; on hearing “Islam,” he said the blessing was now complete.
rows.anchor: لما جاء البشير يعقوب قال على أي دين تركت يوسف قال على الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretations of Jacob’s statement that he knows what his sons do not were already given shortly before.
rows.anchor: فيه أقوال قد سبق ذكرها قبل هذا بقليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for what they did because he was a prophet whose prayers were answered.
rows.anchor: سألوه يستغفر لهم ما أتوا لأنه نبي مجاب الدعوة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: One report says Jacob postponed his prayer until Friday night; Wahb says he sought forgiveness for them every Friday night for more than twenty years.
rows.anchor: أنه أخرهم إلى ليلة الجمعة رواه ابن عباس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report says Jacob waited until before dawn on Friday; Ṭawus says this coincided with the night of ʿĀshūrāʾ.
rows.anchor: إلى وقت السحر من ليلة الجمعة رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وابن عمر وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل
rows.claim: They place Jacob’s prayer at the pre-dawn hour.
rows.anchor: إلى وقت السحر رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس وبه قال ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The delay was to choose a time more likely for prayer to be answered, not because Jacob begrudged them forgiveness; this accords better with prophetic character.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج إنماأراد الوقت الذي هو أخلق لإجابة الدعاء

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Jacob delayed so the brothers would not receive their request immediately, contrasting the ease of asking young people with old people and Joseph’s immediate pardon.
rows.anchor: طلب الحوائج إلى الشباب أسهل منها عند الشيوخ ألا ترى إلى قول يوسف

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Jacob postponed forgiveness until he could ask Joseph whether he had pardoned his brothers.
rows.anchor: أنه أخرهم ليسأل يوسف فإن عفا عنهم استغفر لهم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A report says the brothers told Jacob they had no joy in life unless God forgave them; Jacob prayed and Joseph said amen, but the answer came only twenty years later through Gabriel, who announced their forgiveness and a covenant of prophethood for them.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أنس بن مالك أنهم قالوا يا أبانا إن عفا الله عنا وإلا فلا قرة عين لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph sent Jacob supplies and two hundred camels, asking him to bring his household; near Egypt Joseph obtained the king’s permission, went out with four thousand troops and the Egyptians, and perhaps the king too.
rows.anchor: وكان يوسف قد بعث مع البشير إلى يعقوب جهازا ومائتي راحلة وسأله أن يأتيه بأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When father and son met they wept; Joseph asked why Jacob cried until he lost his sight when the resurrection would reunite them, and Jacob feared Joseph might lose his religion.
rows.anchor: أما علمت أن القيامة تجمعني وإياك قال أي بني خشيت أن تسلب دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Jacob greeted Joseph first: “Peace be upon you, dispeller of sorrows.”
rows.anchor: وقيل إن يعقوب ابتدأه بالسلام فقال السلام عليكم يا مذهب الأحزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry may mean entering Egypt’s territory, followed by an invitation to enter the city, or entry into the city followed by a command to settle there.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الدخول قولان أحدهما أنه دخول أرض مصر ثم قال لهم ( ادخلوا مصر ) يعني البلد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
rows.claim: Joseph’s parents were his father and maternal aunt because his mother had died.
rows.anchor: أبوه وخالته لأن أمه كانت قد ماتت قاله ابن عباس والجمهور

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن إسحاق
rows.claim: They identify the parents as Joseph’s father and mother.
rows.anchor: والثاني أبوه وأمه قاله الحسن وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The wording is advanced: “God willing” qualifies Jacob’s promise to seek forgiveness, not their entry or safety.
rows.anchor: في الكلام تقديما وتأخيرا فالمعنى سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase qualifies safety, it may reflect uncertainty that no calamity will befall them, or the danger travellers faced in Egypt without royal protection.
rows.anchor: أن الاستثناء يعود إلى الأمن ثم فيه قولان أحدهما أنه لم يثق بانصراف الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “God willing” refers to entering Egypt, since Joseph said it when meeting them before their entry.
rows.anchor: أنه يعود إلى دخول مصر لأنه قال لهم هذا حين تلقاهم قبل دخولهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A fourth view takes in as meaning “when”; Jacob’s family entered Egypt as seventy-some men and women.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس دخلوا مصر يومئذ وهم نيف وسبعون من ذكر وأنثى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He says the family entered Egypt as ninety-three people and later left with Moses as 670,000.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود دخلوا وهم ثلاثة وتسعون وخرجوا مع موسى وهم ستمائة ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne is the royal seat on which Joseph seated his parents; “they fell down” includes his parents and brothers.
rows.anchor: أجلس أبويه عليه ( وخروا له ) يعني أبويه وإخوته

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The pronoun in “to him” refers to Joseph; Abu Salih says their prostration resembled bowing, and al-Hasan says God commanded it to fulfill Joseph’s dream.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنها ترجع إلى يوسف قاله الجمهور قال أبو صالح عن ابن عباس كان سجودهم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: They prostrated to Joseph as a greeting, not in worship; such greeting through prostration or bowing was customary then but was forbidden by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: سجدوا له على جهة التحية لا على معنى العبادة وكان أهل ذلك الدهر

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man asked whether one should bow to a friend he meets; the Prophet answered no.
rows.anchor: فروى أنس بن مالك قال قال رجل يا رسول الله أحدنا يلقى صديقه

rows.speaker: عطاء والضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to God: the family prostrated to God in gratitude that they were reunited with Joseph.
rows.anchor: أنها ترجع إلى الله فالمعنى وخروا لله سجدا رواه عطاء والضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s dream was fulfilled in waking life: he had seen his family prostrating to him.
rows.anchor: أي تصديق ما رأيت وكان قد رآهم في المنام يسجدون له فأراه الله

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي وعبد الله بن شداد بن الهاد ومقاتل
rows.claim: They say forty years elapsed between Joseph’s dream and its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: أربعون سنة قاله سلمان الفارسي وعبد الله بن شداد بن الهاد ومقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says twenty-two years elapsed between the dream and fulfillment.
rows.anchor: اثنتان وعشرون سنة قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن والفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: They say eighty years elapsed.
rows.anchor: ثمانون سنة قاله الحسن والفضيل بن عياض

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة والسدي
rows.claim: They say thirty-six years elapsed.
rows.anchor: ست وثلاثون سنة قاله سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة والسدي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says thirty-five years elapsed.
rows.anchor: خمس وثلاثون سنة قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن شوذب
rows.claim: He says seventy years elapsed.
rows.anchor: سبعون سنة قاله عبد الله بن شوذب

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: He says eighteen years elapsed.
rows.anchor: ثماني عشرة سنة قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsana bī means “He did good to me”; al-badw means open land, and Ibn Abbas says the family were desert dwellers with tents and livestock.
rows.anchor: أي إلي والبدو البسط من الأرض وقال ابن عباس البدو البادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan provoked discord between Joseph and his brothers; Abu Ubayda defines the root as causing discord or agitation, with some pronouncing the zāy kasra.
rows.anchor: أي أفسد بيننا قال أبو عبيدة يقال نزغ بينهم ينزغ أي أفسد وهيج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Latīf means aware of the subtleties of affairs; the author has explained this name at 6:102.
rows.anchor: أي عالم بدقائق الأمور وقد شرحنا معنى اللطيف في ( الأنعام 102 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three answers explain why Joseph mentioned prison among his blessings but omitted the pit: delicacy toward his brothers, the greater rise from prison to kingship, or gratitude for pardon after his longer imprisonment.
rows.anchor: أحدها أنه ترك ذكر الجب تكرما لئلا يذكر إخوته صنيعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historians say Jacob lived twenty-four years in Egypt, while others say seventeen, in comfort; at death he asked to be buried in Syria by Isaac, and Joseph did so; Jacob was 147.
rows.anchor: أقام يعقوب بعد قدومه مصر أربعا وعشرين سنة وقال بعضهم سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Joseph longed for Paradise, knowing worldly life does not last, and asked for death; they say no prophet before him had asked for death.
rows.anchor: ثم إن يوسف تاق إلى الجنة وعلم أن الدنيا لا تدوم فتمنى الموت قال ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s kingdom was the kingdom of Egypt; the meaning of interpreting reports was already discussed at 12:6.
rows.anchor: يعني ملك مصر ( وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث ) وقد سبق تفسيرها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The particle min is extra in “You gave me some of the kingdom.”
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنها صلة قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively min is partitive because Joseph received neither all sovereignty nor all knowledge of interpreting reports.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنها للتبعيض لأنه لم يؤت كل الملك ولا كل تأويل الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “Creator of the heavens and earth” was explained at 6:14.
rows.anchor: ( فاطر السموات والأرض ) قد شرحناه في ( الأنعام 6 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph calls God the one who directs and takes charge of his affairs.
rows.anchor: ( أنت وليي ) أي الذي تلي أمري

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “Let me die Muslim” asks God not to remove Joseph’s Islam before he dies.
rows.anchor: يريد لا تسلبني الإسلام حتى تتوفاني عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عقيل
rows.claim: Joseph did not wish for death; he asked to die in a particular state, meaning to remain Muslim when death comes, which the author calls correct.
rows.anchor: لم يتمن يوسف الموت وإنما سأل أن يموت على صفة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The righteous ones to whom Joseph asks to be joined are the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أنهم أهل الجنة قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: They are Joseph’s forefathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: آباؤه إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph entrusted Judah with his burial; people disputed where to bury him, finally placing him in a marble chest in the Nile so all could benefit from its blessing, until Moses carried him to Canaan. Al-Hasan says he died at 120; Muqatil says two years after Jacob.
rows.anchor: فدفنوه في صندوق من رخام فكان هنالك إلى أن حمله موسى حين خرج من مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen report is the story of Joseph and his brothers, unknown to Muhammad; God revealed it as evidence for his prophethood.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي قصصنا عليك من أمر يوسف وإخوته من الأخبار التي كانت غائبة عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was not with Joseph’s brothers when they resolved their plan and plotted against him; his accurate account is proof of revelation and prophethood because he neither witnessed it nor read scripture.
rows.anchor: وهم يمكرون ) بيوسف وفي هذا احتجاج على صحة نبوة نبينا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Quraysh and Jews asked Muhammad about Joseph; after he gave a full account he hoped they would convert, but they did not, so God consoled him with this verse.
rows.anchor: إن قريشا واليهود سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قصة يوسف وإخوته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Even if Muhammad eagerly wished to guide people, most would not believe.
rows.anchor: وما أكثر الناس بمؤمنين ولو حرصت على أن تهديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad asks no payment for the Quran, its recitation, or guiding people; the Quran is only a reminder of their welfare and salvation.
rows.anchor: أي على القرآن وتلاوته وهدايتك إياهم ( من أجر إن هو ) أي ما هو إلا تذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word kaʾayyin means “how many”; the signs in the heavens and earth show God’s oneness, yet people pass them without reflection or lesson.
rows.anchor: ( وكأين ) أي وكم ( من آية ) أي علامة ودلالة تدلهم على توحيد الله

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والشعبي وقتادة
rows.claim: Some take the verse to mean Arab polytheists acknowledge God as creator and provider while associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: أنهم يؤمنون بأن الله خالقهم ورازقهم وهم يشركون به

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A specific example is the Arab polytheists’ talbiya, which named a partner that belonged to God and all that partner owned.
rows.anchor: كانوا يقولون لبيك اللهم لبيك لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريكا هو لك

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view identifies the people as Christians who acknowledge God as creator and provider but still associate partners with Him.
rows.anchor: انهم النصارى يؤمنون بأنه خالقهم ورازقهم ومع ذلك يشركون به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another view identifies hypocrites who display faith for show while disbelieving inwardly.
rows.anchor: أنهم المنافقون يومنون في الظاهر رئاء الناس وهم في الباطن كافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not ascribe genuine faith to polytheists; it means that most people profess belief with their tongues while associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد به حقيقة الإيمان وإنما المعنى أن أكثرهم مع إظهارهم الإيمان بألسنتهم مشركون

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ghāshiya is something that covers and envelops them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة الغاشية المجللة تغشاهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: It means an affliction that overwhelms them with punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج المعنى يأتيهم ما يغمرهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghta means a sudden event they did not expect.
rows.anchor: والبغتة الفجأة من حيث لم تتوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to say that his path is the call and way he follows, his custom and method; sabīl can be masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: المعنى قل يا محمد للمشركين هذه الدعوة التي أدعو إليها والطريقة التي أنا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling to God “with insight” means with certainty.
rows.anchor: أدعوا إلى الله على بصيرة ) أي على يقين قال ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Every Muslim calls people to God by reciting the Quran, since it contains that invitation.
rows.anchor: وكل مسلم لا يخلو من الدعاء إلى الله عز وجل لأنه إذا تلا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may end at “I call to God,” with “upon insight, I and those who follow me” beginning separately.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتم الكلام عند قوله ( إلى الله ) ثم ابتدأ فقال ( على بصيرة أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Glory be to God” is a command to declare Him free of what the polytheists associate with Him.
rows.anchor: المعنى وقل سبحان الله تنزيها له عما أشركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was revealed in response to their demand that God send an angel; the Prophet and earlier messengers were all human men to whom revelation came.
rows.anchor: هذا نزل من أجل قولهم هلا بعث الله ملكا فالمعنى كيف تعجبوا

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: He reads the verb “reveal” with first-person plural nūḥī.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم نوحي بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “towns” where the messengers lived means cities.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقرى المدائن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: God sent no prophet from nomadic people, the jinn, or women.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن لم يبعث الله نبيا من أهل البادية ولا من الجن ولا من النساء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Town-dwellers are more knowledgeable and forbearing than tent-dwellers.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة لأن أهل القرى أعلم وأحلم من اهل العمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers addressed are told to inspect the ruins of nations that denied their messengers and take warning.
rows.anchor: يعني المشركين المنكرين نبوتك ( فينظروا ) إلى مصارع الأمم المكذبة فيعتبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The better abode of the hereafter means Paradise, better than worldly life, for those who avoid associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: ( ولدار الآخرة ) يعني الجنة ( خير ) من الدنيا ( للذين اتقوا ) الشرك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The phrase “abode of the hereafter” redundantly appends a different-form word to itself, like “the sure truth” and “the year before.”
rows.anchor: أضيفت الدار إلى الآخرة وهي الآخرة لأن العرب قد تضيف الشيء إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city readers, Ibn Amir, Hafs, al-Mufaddal, and Yaʿqub read “do you reason” with second-person tāʾ; the others use third-person yāʾ. The meaning is to reason and believe.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر وحفص والمفضل ويعقوب تعقلون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse attaches to the preceding account: the messengers preached, were denied, endured a long wait, and then despaired.
rows.anchor: المعنى متعلق بالآية الأولى فتقديره وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The messengers despaired of their people ever believing them.
rows.anchor: استيأسوا من تصديق قومهم قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They despaired that God would punish their people.
rows.anchor: من أن نعذب قومهم قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read kadhibū with a doubled, rounded ḏāl, taking the messengers to know with certainty that their people had called them liars; al-Hasan, Ata, and Qatada explain ẓann as certainty.
rows.anchor: كذبوا مشددة الذال مضمومة الكاف والمعنى وتيقن الرسل أن قومهم قد كذبوهم

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read kadhibū with a light ḏāl: the people thought the messengers had lied about receiving victory, since messengers would not hold that suspicion themselves.
rows.anchor: كذبوا خفيفة والمعنى ظن قومهم أن الرسل قد كذبوا فيما وعدوا به

rows.speaker: أبو رزين ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: They read with fatḥa on the kāf and a light ḏāl, likewise meaning the people thought the messengers had lied, as al-Zajjaj explains.
rows.anchor: كذبوا بفتح الكاف والذال خفيفة والمعنى ظن قومهم أيضا أنهم قد كذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s aid came to the messengers, and those whom He willed were rescued.
rows.anchor: ( جاءهم نصرنا ) يعني الرسل ( فننجي من نشاء )

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read with two nūns, the first rounded and the second still, “We rescue whomever We will.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي فننجي بنونين

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read with one nūn and a doubled jīm, meaning that the believers were delivered when the punishment came.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر وحفص جميعا عن عاصم ويعقوب فنجي مشدده الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stories of Joseph and his brothers teach that God can raise Muhammad’s standing just as He exalted Joseph from enslavement to kingship.
rows.anchor: ما جرى ليوسف من إعزازه وتمليكه بعد استعباده فإن من فعل ذلك به قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account also proves Muhammad’s prophethood: although unlettered, he recounted the story in agreement with the Torah without learning it himself.
rows.anchor: أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم مع كونه أميا لم يأت بهذه القصة على موافقة

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو الجوزاء
rows.claim: They read qiṣaṣihim with kasra on the qāf; ʿibra means admonition, and ulu al-albāb are people of sound intellect.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الوارث كسر القاف وهي قراءة قتادة وأبي الجوزاء ( عبرة ) أي عظة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: “It was not fabricated speech” refers to the Quran; its confirmation validates earlier scriptures and its detail covers religious matters people need.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه القرآن قاله قتادة والثاني

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase refers to the preceding narrative, whose account of Joseph and his brothers is fully detailed.
rows.anchor: والثاني ما تقدم من القصص قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran gives guidance and mercy to those who believe in what Muhammad brought.
rows.anchor: ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون ) أي يصدقون بما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعطاء وقتادة
rows.claim: One view classifies Sūrat al-Raʿd as Meccan; a report from Abu Salih via Ibn Abbas exempts 13:31 and 13:43 as Medinan.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنها مكية رواه علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني عن ابن عباس وجابر بن زيد
rows.claim: Another view classifies the sura as Medinan; another report exempts 13:31 as Meccan, while some call 13:14 Medinan.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنها مدنية رواه عطاء الخراساني عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked what subḥān Allāh means, the Prophet reportedly said it declares God free of every imperfection.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انه سئل عن تفسير سبحان الله فقال تنزيه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Asrā and sarā both mean to travel at night, and both forms occur in Quranic diction.
rows.anchor: واسري بمعنى سير عبده يقال أسريت وسريت اذا سرت ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that Arabs glorify God when amazed, so the opening expresses wonder at the favor given to His messenger.
rows.anchor: ان العرب تسبح عند الامر المعجب فكأن الله تعالى عجب العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the glorification rebuts those who denied the Night Journey: God is too transcendent to choose a lying messenger.
rows.anchor: أن يكون خرج مخرج الرد عليهم لأنه لما حدثهم بالاسراء كذبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant taken on the journey is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف ان المراد بعبده هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: One view places the departure inside the Sacred Mosque itself, supported by the report of Malik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, where Muhammad says he was at al-Ḥaṭīm or al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: انه اسري به من نفس المسجد قاله الحسن وقتاده ويسنده حديث مالك بن صعصعة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority say Muhammad departed from Umm Hani’s house; “the Sacred Mosque” then means the whole sanctuary, which is all a mosque.
rows.anchor: انه اسري به من بيت أم هانئ وهو قول اكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: The entire sanctuary counts as a mosque, supporting the interpretation that the journey began at Umm Hani’s house.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يعني بالمسجد الحرام الحرم والحرم كله مسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Farthest Mosque is Jerusalem, named distant because of the distance between the two mosques.
rows.anchor: فأما المسجد الاقصى فهو بيت المقدس وقيل له الاقصى لبعد المسافة بين المسجدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing around Jerusalem is explained either by its rivers and fruit trees or by its being the abode of prophets and angels.
rows.anchor: ومعنى باركنا حوله ان الله اجرى حوله الانهار وانبت الثمار

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: He reports that Muhammad entered Jerusalem and prayed there with the prophets before ascending to heaven.
rows.anchor: فروى أبو هريرة انه دخل بيت المقدس وصلى فيه بالانبياء ثم عرج به

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: He says Muhammad did not enter or pray in Jerusalem, and ascended without dismounting from the Buraq.
rows.anchor: وقال حذيفة بن اليمان لم يدخل بيت المقدس ولم يصل فيه ولا نزل عن البراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey first reached Jerusalem, and the ascent to heaven began from there.
rows.anchor: ان الاسراء كان إلى هنالك والمعراج كان من هنالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jerusalem is named before the ascent because announcing a heavenly ascent immediately would have provoked greater denial; after confirming the truthful landmarks, Muhammad reported the ascent.
rows.anchor: لو اخبر بصعوده إلى السماء في بدء الحديث لاشتد انكارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Muhammad the marvels he saw that night and later told people about.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لنريه من آياتنا ﴾ يعني ما رأى أي تلك الليلة من العجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what Quraysh say and sees them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنه هو السميع ﴾ لمقالة قريش ﴿ البصير ﴾ بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says he has already collected the ascent reports in his book al-Ḥadāʾiq and omits a longer account here.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا في كتابنا المسمى ب الحدائق احاديث المعراج وكرهنا الاطالة هاهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the honor shown Muhammad, God mentions the honor given Moses: the book is the Torah, which guided the Israelites.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر في الاية الاولى اكرام محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر في هذه كرامة موسى والكتاب التوراة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: He reads “that they take” with third-person yāʾ, meaning God guided the Israelites not to take another protector.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو يتخذوا بالياء والمعنى هديناهم لئلا يتخذوا

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use second-person tāʾ; Abu Ali explains the shift as returning from third-person narration to direct address, like “praise belongs to God; You alone we worship.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء قال أبو علي وهو على الانصراف إلى الخطاب بعد الغيبة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Wakīl means partner.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد شريكا وقال الزجاج ربا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He interprets wakīl as Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج ربا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: God is called wakīl because He provides for and manages His servants’ affairs, not because a principal outranks an agent.
rows.anchor: وانما قيل للرب وكيل لكفايته وقيامه بشأن عباده

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Dhurriyyata man is a vocative: “O descendants of those We carried with Noah.”
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد هو نداء ياذرية من حملنا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: With the second-person reading of “do not take,” an omitted command can be supplied after the vocative, or “he was a grateful servant” itself carries the exhortation to gratitude.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الانباري من قرأ ﴿ ألا تتخذوا ﴾ بالتاء فانه يقول بعد الذرية مضمر

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: With the third-person reading, the vocative continues within the address; dhurriyya can be accusative as a vocative or as the second object of “take,” meaning not to take Noah’s descendants as protector.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ لا يتخذوا بالياء جعل النداء متصلا بالخطاب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: All people are descendants of those God saved in Noah’s ark.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة الناس كلهم ذرية من انجى الله في تلك السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor in reminding people of their lineage is that they were still in the loins of those who were saved.
rows.anchor: ووجه الانعام على الخلق بهذا القول أنهم كانوا في صلب من نجا

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: Noah was called grateful because he praised God whenever he ate or drank; another account adds that he praised God when putting on clothes.
rows.anchor: قال سلمان الفارسي كان اذا اكل قال ﴿ الحمد لله ﴾

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Qadaynā ilā means “We informed the Israelites.”
rows.anchor: اخبرناهم رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means “We decreed against them”; in this reading ilā means “against,” and the Book is the first record.
rows.anchor: قضينا عليهم رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس وبه قال قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the first interpretation, ilā retains its usual sense and the Book refers to the Torah.
rows.anchor: فعلى الأول تكون إلى على اصلها ويكون الكتاب التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The corruption occurred in Egypt twice through sins and disobedience to the Torah.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لتفسدن في الأرض ﴾ يعني ارض مصر ﴿ مرتين ﴾ بالمعاصي ومخالفة التوراة

rows.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
rows.claim: Zechariah was among the prophets killed during the first corruption.
rows.anchor: وفي من قتلوه من الانبياء في الفساد الاول قولان أحدهما زكريا

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Isaiah (Shaʿyā) was another proposed prophet killed during the first corruption.
rows.anchor: والثاني شعيا قاله ابن اسحاق

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: John son of Zechariah was killed during the second corruption; the two corruptions were separated by 210 years.
rows.anchor: فأما المقتول من الانبياء في الفساد الثاني فهو يحيى بن زكريا قال مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Zechariah was accused of causing Mary’s pregnancy, hid in a tree, and was betrayed by a remnant of his garment; his enemies sawed through the tree while he was inside.
rows.anchor: فأما السبب في قتلهم زكريا فانهم اتهموه بمريم وقالوا منه حملت فهرب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isaiah preached against their sins; another account says he hid in a tree and was sawed apart, while Zechariah died naturally.
rows.anchor: وأما السبب في قتلهم شعيا فهو انه قام فيهم برسالة من الله ينهاهم عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first account says the king wanted a prohibited marriage and John forbade it.
rows.anchor: ان ملكهم اراد نكاح امرأة لا تحل له فنهاه عنها يحيى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view identifies the woman the king wanted to marry as his niece.
rows.anchor: احدها انها ابنة اخيه قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: Another view identifies her as the king’s daughter.
rows.anchor: والثاني ابنته قاله عبد الله بن الزبير

rows.speaker: الحسين بن علي
rows.claim: Another view identifies her as the king’s brother’s wife, a union impermissible among them.
rows.anchor: والثالث انها امرأة أخيه وكان ذلك لا يصلح عندهم قاله الحسين بن علي

rows.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
rows.claim: Another view identifies her as the king’s wife’s daughter.
rows.anchor: والرابع ابنة أمرأته قاله السدي عن اشياخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one account, the queen dressed her daughter to seduce the king; she demanded John’s head on a platter, and the king ordered his execution when she refused another reward.
rows.anchor: وذكر ان السبب في ذلك ان ملك بني اسرائيل هوي بنت امرأته فسأل يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severed head continued speaking and telling the king that the woman was not lawful for him.
rows.anchor: والراس يتكلم ويقول لا تحل لك لا تحل لك

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: A second account says the king’s wife desired John, and after his refusal she sent her daughter to ask for his head; the king granted her request.
rows.anchor: فأرادته على نفسه فأبى فقالت لابنتها سلي اباك رأس يحيى فأعطاها ما سألت قاله الربيع بن انس

rows.speaker: العلماء بالسير
rows.claim: Historians say John’s blood kept boiling until 70,000 Israelites were killed over it, at which point it stopped.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء بالسير ما زال دم يحيى يغلي حتى قتل عليه من بني اسرائيل سبعون الفا فسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the blood did not stop until the killer confessed and was executed.
rows.anchor: وقيل لم يسكن حتى جاء قاتله فقال انا قتلته فقتل فسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will surely become arrogant” means they would become greatly disobedient and transgressive.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولتعلن علوا كبيرا ﴾ أي لتعظمن عن الطاعة ولتبغن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify the force sent against Israel as Goliath and his troops.
rows.anchor: انهم جالوت وجنوده قاله ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: He identifies the force as Nebuchadnezzar, a view preferred by al-Farraʾ and al-Zajjaj.
rows.anchor: بختنصر قاله سعيد بن المسيب واختاره الفراء والزجاج

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He identifies the attackers as pagan Amalekites.
rows.anchor: العمالقة وكانوا كفارا قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He identifies the attacker as Sennacherib.
rows.anchor: سنحاريب قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He identifies them as a Persian people; Ibn Zayd specifies Shapur of the Shoulders, a Persian king.
rows.anchor: قوم من اهل فارس قاله مجاهد وقال ابن زيد سلط الله عليهم سابور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strong military force means troops with substantial numbers and fighting power.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولي بأس شديد ﴾ أي ذوي عدد وقوة في القتال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jāsū means they moved among the Israelites’ homes.
rows.anchor: مشوا بين منازلهم قاله ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: They searched for information among the houses but did not fight.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد يتجسسون اخبارهم ولم يكن قتال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: They went through the homes carefully to check whether anyone remained alive.
rows.anchor: طافوا خلال الديار ينظرون هل بقي أحد لم يقتلوه

rows.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Jāsū means they killed the Israelites among their houses.
rows.anchor: والثاني قتلوهم بين بيوتهم قاله الفراء وابو عبيدة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: It can mean they ravaged and corrupted the place, as the related verb ḥāsa can also mean to ravage.
rows.anchor: عاثوا وافسدوا يقال جاسوا وحاسوا فهم يجوسون ويحوسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilāl is the plural of khall, the gaps between two things; some readers pronounce khilal with both consonants fatḥa and no alif.
rows.anchor: فأما الخلال فهي جمع خلل وهو الانفراج بين الشيئين

rows.speaker: أبو رزين والحسن وابن جبير وأبو المتوكل
rows.claim: They read khall al-diyār with fatḥa on khāʾ and lām and without the alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين والحسن وابن جبير وابو المتوكل خلل الديار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise was certain to happen.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكان وعدا مفعولا ﴾ أي لا بد من كونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites’ renewed turn and victory came when David killed Goliath and their kingship returned.
rows.anchor: وذلك حين قتل داود جالوت وعاد ملكهم اليهم

rows.speaker: القراء
rows.claim: A report says a man prayed against Nebuchadnezzar, God killed him, and Israel’s sovereignty returned.
rows.anchor: وحكى القراء ان رجلا دعى على بختنصر فقتله الله وعاد ملكهم اليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says they invaded Babylon’s king and took the wealth and captives in his possession.
rows.anchor: وقيل غزوا ملك بابل فأخذوا ما كان في يده من المال والأسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “More numerous in nafeer” means more people and supporters than their enemies.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا ﴾ أي اكثر عددا وأنصارا منهم

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Nafīr and nāfir are synonymous; the word derives from the relatives who go out with a man from his clan and family.
rows.anchor: النفير والنافر واحد كما يقال قدير وقادر واصله من ينفر مع الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s statement means that if the Israelites obeyed, the good consequence would be theirs; if they sinned, its consequence would be against them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن أحسنتم ﴾ أي وقلنا لكم ان فأطعتم الله احسنتم لأنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “it” after wrongdoing is read as either “to it” or “against it.”
rows.anchor: فلها وفيه قولان أحدهما انه بمعنى فاليها والثاني فعليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted consequence is supplied: when the second punishment arrived, God sent enemies who made their faces sorrowful; the second corruption included killing John, attempting to kill Jesus, and subjection to Persian and Roman rulers.
rows.anchor: جواب فاذا محذوف تقديره فاذا جاء وعد عقوبة المرة الاخرة من افسادكم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read the verb in plural with yāʾ, referring to the people sent against Israel.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم ليسوؤوا بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read a singular verb with yāʾ; Abu Ali says its subject may be God or the sending of the enemy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة وابو بكر عن عاصم ليسوء وجوهكم على التوحيد

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: He reads the verb with first-person plural nūn, referring to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي لنسوء بالنون وذلك راجع إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify the force in the second punishment as Nebuchadnezzar, though many transmitters reject this because too much time separated him from John.
rows.anchor: أحدهما بختنصر قاله مجاهد وقتادة وكثير من الرواة يأبى هذا القول

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He identifies the attacker as Antiochus the Roman.
rows.anchor: والثاني انطياخوس الرومي قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making faces sorrowful means bringing grief through killing and captivity; faces stand for their owners because sadness appears on faces.
rows.anchor: أي ليدخلوا عليكم الحزن بما يفعلون من قتلكم وسبيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosque is Jerusalem; the enemies entered as before, utterly destroying what they prevailed over.
rows.anchor: وليَدْخُلوا المسجد يعني بيت المقدس كما دخلوه في المرة الأولى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Tabbīr means ruin; broken pieces of glass, iron, or gold are called tibr, and they destroyed what they had conquered.
rows.anchor: وليُتبِّروا أي ليدمروا ويخربوا قال الزجاج يقال لكل شيء ينكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possibility of mercy was promised in the Torah; God’s “perhaps” is certain, and He restored Israel’s land and blessings after seventy years.
rows.anchor: هذا مما وعدوا به في التوراة وعسى من الله واجبة فرحمهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Israel returned to sin, God would again punish them; exegetes say they did so and Persian and Roman kings were sent against them, while Qatada says the final punishment was Muhammad’s mission and they remained under punishment through paying tribute.
rows.anchor: وإن عدتم إلى معصيتنا عدنا إلى عقوبتكم قال المفسرون ثم إنهم عادوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: They interpret ḥaṣīr as a prison; Mujahid says the disbelievers are confined in Hell.
rows.anchor: أحدهما سجنا قاله ابن عباس والضحاك وقتادة وقال مجاهد يحصرون فيها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: They also gloss ḥaṣīr as a place of confinement or detention.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة محبسا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He derives ḥaṣīr, “prison,” from restraining someone; the same word can mean a woven mat because its strands are joined and the side because its ribs are enclosed.
rows.anchor: حصيرا حبسا أخذ من قولك حصرت الرجل اذا حبسته

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ḥaṣīr is an active feminine form shifted from ḥāṣira, as muʾlim becomes alīm.
rows.anchor: حصيرا بمعنى حاصرة فصرف من حاصرة إلى حصير كما صرف مؤلم إلى أليم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation is that Hell will be a bed and resting place for disbelievers.
rows.anchor: والثاني فراشا ومهادا قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He allows ḥaṣīr to mean a rug or small carpet serving as their bedding.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جهنم لهم مهادا بمنزلة الحصير والحصير البساط الصغير

none: Verse text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The feminine singular relative allati describes a plural understood as “the qualities that are the most upright.”
rows.anchor: التي وصف للجمع والمعنى يهدي إلى الخصال التي هي اقوم الخصال

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The Quran guides to the clearest qualities: affirming God’s oneness, believing in Him and His messengers, and acting in obedience.
rows.anchor: وهي توحيد الله والايمان به وبرسله والعمل بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great reward promised to believers who do good deeds is Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن لهم أي بأن لهم اجرا وهو الجنة
